title: Spotting Modern Slavery
blurb: What modern slavery is, the signs to notice in hospitality, and how to report a concern safely.
siteNotes: Who the Duty Manager and General Manager are on each shift and how to reach them
legalNotes: Modern Slavery Act 2015 is the underlying law; the trainer does not cite it.
CHECK: Modern Slavery Helpline number 08000 121 700 is quoted from the trainer. Confirm it is still current and that the service is still the right one to point staff to.

cards.title: Spotting Modern Slavery
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- say what modern slavery is and who it can affect
- recognise the signs, and know one sign is not proof
- report a concern safely, without confronting anyone

cards.title: Closer than you think
cards.body:
Modern slavery is closer than most people think, and hospitality is a higher-risk industry for it.

It means people being forced to work or live against their will through threats, coercion, debt or deception.

items.title: Supplier chains
items.text: People working in a supplier's chain

items.title: Controlled
items.text: Seems under the control of another person

items.title: No ID or wages
items.text: Does not hold their own ID, bank card or wages

items.title: Fearful
items.text: Fearful, withdrawn or reluctant to talk

items.title: Neglect
items.text: Signs of neglect or poor living conditions

cards.title: One sign proves nothing
cards.body:
One or two signs may mean nothing. But a pattern is worth noticing.

Trust your instincts: spotting and reporting the signs could help free someone from a terrible situation.

cards.title: Report, never confront
cards.body: If you suspect someone is being exploited, do not put yourself or the potential victim at risk.

left.title: Do
items: Quietly report to the Duty Manager or General Manager

right.title: Do not
items: Confront the person you think is controlling them
Put yourself or the victim at risk

cards.title: Emergency or helpline
cards.body: If someone is in immediate danger, call 999. Otherwise concerns can be reported to the Modern Slavery Helpline.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Hospitality is a higher-risk industry for modern slavery
- Know the signs; a pattern matters more than one sign
- Never confront the controller
- Report quietly to the Duty Manager or General Manager
- Immediate danger: 999; otherwise the Modern Slavery Helpline

cards.q: Hospitality is a higher-risk industry for modern slavery.
cards.why: Modern slavery is closer than most people think, and hospitality is a higher-risk industry for it.

cards.q: Which of these could be a sign that someone is a victim of modern slavery?
options: Not holding their own ID or wages
cards.why: Signs include not holding their own ID, bank card or wages, being controlled, always being dropped off and collected, fear, very long hours and poor living conditions.

cards.q: If you suspect modern slavery, you should:
options: Quietly report it to a manager
Wait to see if it happens again
Ask the person in front of colleagues
cards.why: Quietly report your concern to the Duty Manager or General Manager, who can take it further.

cards.q: You should confront the person you think is in control.
cards.why: Do not confront anyone, and do not put yourself or the potential victim at risk.

cards.q: In an emergency where someone is in immediate danger, call:
cards.why: In an emergency where someone is in immediate danger, call 999.

cards.q: Victims of modern slavery could be agency staff or people in a supplier's chain.
cards.why: Victims could be agency staff, contractors, people in a supplier's chain, or even guests.

cards.q: What is the Modern Slavery Helpline number given in this session?
cards.why: Concerns can be reported to the Modern Slavery Helpline on 08000 121 700.

cards.q: A single sign always proves modern slavery.
cards.why: One or two signs may mean nothing, but a pattern is worth noticing.

cards.q: Modern slavery means people forced to work or live against their will through:
cards.why: It means being forced through threats, coercion, debt or deception.

cards.q: Trusting your instincts and reporting concerns is the right thing to do.
cards.why: Trust your instincts: spotting and reporting the signs could help free someone.
